title: Prophecy
description: One prophecy record (the stored, append-only form).

expires_at.description: Expiry: after this instant the prophecy may no longer be resolved — the sweep moves it to `Expired`.

fulfilment.description: The fulfilment, once it happens. Terminal.

requires_human.description: False ONLY for deterministic Findings from a reader. Model- and human-produced prophecies carry true; the store REJECTS a `false` from a non-Reader producer (fail closed).

Fulfilment.description: How a prophecy ended. Terminal: a fulfilled or dismissed prophecy is never re-resolved.

note.description: Free-text note (the operator's or producer's reason).

state.description: The terminal state this prophecy ended in.

oneOf.description: A deterministic observation from a reader: a structured fact about some watched state. No inference.

payload.description: The finding's payload — the reader's structured output (rows, counts, matched shapes). Opaque to this crate.

oneOf.description: A drafted response to a finding. A model product; the text itself, never a dispatch.

finding.description: The finding this drafts a response to.

oneOf.description: A suggested action with its recipe shape. A proposal — nothing executes it.

rationale.description: Why the model suggests it (bounded, recorded).

recipe.description: The recipe (or named procedure) the action proposes.

oneOf.description: An improvement proposal pointing at a configuration target with evidence. NOTHING applies it — a human edits the file.

proposal.description: The proposed change, as text or a patch-shaped object.

target.description: The target it points at (a file, section, or config key).

Producer.description: What produced this prophecy — the trust tier of the derivation.

oneOf.description: A deterministic reader (configured code, no inference). The only producer that may set `requires_human: false`.
A model over collected findings (resident or external). Always `requires_human: true`.

Provenance.description: The origin of one observation a prophecy was derived from — the audit trail. Host systems fill these fields from their own records; the crate only requires they be present.

event_log_seq.description: The host's log sequence number for that observation — the prophecy points INTO the durable log.

observation_hash.description: The observation's content hash — the exact state the evidence was read from (whatever hash the host records).

Source.description: A deterministic watch target's identity — where a finding came from (a configured source id plus its stable identity).

id.description: The configured source's id (the watcher's own name for it).

row_hash.description: The full-row hash — the evidence for THIS row of the finding (row contents hashed; any content change is a new evidence value).

row_key.description: The finding's stable ROW identity as the reader defines it (e.g. sender+subject+received for a message list, or a natural key for any row-shaped source). Readers key their emissions on this so a host can deduplicate and coalesce.

State.description: The terminal state of a resolved prophecy.

oneOf.description: The proposal's gated task ran to completion. This is a RECORD of completion, never an instruction.
Removed by the expiry sweep (not a choice anyone made).
